challenge.better_approach: Considered running dc945's verdict on Windows: measured impossible there today (no bubblewrap, akiendell_cc_0's 8610 verdict attempt), and that is 86cccb7d30f7's bigger cure, still at TICKETME. Considered teaching the hypothesis to expect exit 1 on Linux: that would make the instrument pass a hollow build too (Law 8). Calling the one existing reader from the one place that disposes is the smallest change.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the run record the gate holds carries fail_lines: verdict.run_instrument builds it at verdict.py:262 from stdout lines starting with FAIL, and the measured Linux output of bin/proofs/test_cairn_resolves_from_powershell.py prints exactly two such lines, both UNRAN. A runner that omits fail_lines must stay killed (host_bound_reading returns None for a non-list).
challenge.prior_art: 50ac45cde4dd (PROVED) built host_bound_reading and wired it into verdict.py:566 only, the door's criterion re-run; its bounds named chart stages as out. 86cccb7d30f7 (TICKETME) has gate.py in its bounds but asks the sealer on a box without bubblewrap, a different host and path. 7cae18f7f9c2 (berths resolved by commons copy) touched _dispose for berth paths only. Grepped tickets, questions and ideas for _dispose and host_bound: no ticket covers this.
challenge.real_collision: 86cccb7d30f7 also writes gate.py; distinction, not collision: it changes where the verdict runs on a box without bubblewrap, this changes how a failed run on a box WITH it is read. Both can stand. RULE 1 holds: verdict is a machine in the same device (codemother), and gate.py already imports it as V.

answers.falsifier: With an injected run whose fail lines are all UNRAN and a green seal on these bytes naming those teeth green, _dispose returns confirmed with host_read; with any non-UNRAN fail line, or no seal on these bytes, it stays killed; a run exiting 0 is confirmed with no host_read. Horizon: dc945eb1f072's Linux verdict confirms. Wrong intent if the verdict must run on the host that can run the tooth (then 86cccb7d30f7's sealer dial is the cure, not this).
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured, not imagined: CairnCommons/berths/chart/verdict-20261123T041756-04743f0c2382.json is dc945eb1f072's killed verdict, 2026-11-23
answers.how: In cairn/devices/codemother/machines/chart_gate/gate.py StageGate._dispose, a run that did not exit 0 (and did not time out) is passed to verdict's published host_bound_reading(command, run['fail_lines']); a non-None reading disposes the hypothesis confirmed and carries host_read beside it, None leaves it killed. A red-first proof beside the gate injects a runner whose run fails with UNRAN teeth only and a scratch proof with a green seal on these bytes.
answers.traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured: the seal from the host that can run the tooth IS the measurement, and the gate discards it) and Law 8 (the proof gates entry to proven-space; a gate that cannot read a valid proof makes a host-bound component unprovable). Sibling of 50ac45cde4dd, which fixed the same read at the verdict door only.
answers.what: The verdict gate's disposition of a hypothesis whose instrument fails only on teeth this host cannot run reads the seal a host that could run them took on these bytes, the way the verdict door already does, so a Windows-only proof can reach PROVED from the Linux verdict.

bullets.text: 50ac45cde4dd fixed host-bound teeth at one of the verdict's two judges: the door's criterion re-run reads the seal from the host that can run it, but the chart gate's _dispose re-runs every hypothesis instrument itself and kills on any nonzero exit, so dc945eb1f072 (a Windows-only proof) was killed on Linux with a green Windows seal on these bytes standing.
8610b4aa2477 was not blocked by this: its proof exits 0 on Linux (the nt tooth reports but does not fail), so only its hollow needed the Windows host.

title: The verdict gate's disposition of a hypothesis whose instrument fails only on teeth this host cannot run reads the seal
